title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
abstract: Large pre-trained language models store factual knowledge in their parameters and achieve state-of-the-art results when combined with non-parametric retrieval memory.
main_finding: RAG models generate more specific, diverse, and factual language than parametric-only baselines.

title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
abstract: ReAct prompts large language models to generate both verbal reasoning traces and task-specific actions in an interleaved manner.
main_finding: Interleaving chain-of-thought reasoning with external tool actions significantly reduces hallucination and improves task success rates.

title: Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools
abstract: Toolformer is a model trained to decide which APIs to call, when to call them, what arguments to pass, and how to best incorporate results into future token prediction.
main_finding: Self-supervised tool learning enables smaller language models to outperform much larger models on arithmetic and factual lookup tasks.

title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
abstract: Self-RAG trains an arbitrary LM to adaptively retrieve passages on-demand and reflect on retrieved passages and its own generations using reflection tokens.
main_finding: On-demand retrieval and self-reflection tokens outperform standard RAG on factuality and citation accuracy.

title: AgentBench: Evaluating LLMs as Agents Across Diverse Environments
abstract: AgentBench is a multi-dimensional benchmark designed to evaluate LLM-as-Agent reasoning and decision-making abilities across 8 distinct environments.
main_finding: Long-horizon reasoning, strict instruction following, and tool error recovery remain primary bottlenecks for open-weight agent models.

title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models
abstract: Generating a chain of thought—a series of intermediate reasoning steps—significantly improves the ability of large language models to perform complex arithmetic and symbolic reasoning.
main_finding: Intermediate reasoning demonstrations unlock emergent multi-step problem solving in sufficiently large language models.

title: Gorilla: Large Language Model Connected with Massive APIs
abstract: Gorilla is a finetuned LLaMA-based model that surpasses GPT-4 on writing API calls and adapts dynamically to API documentation changes using retriever-aware training.
main_finding: Retriever-aware training substantially reduces API argument hallucinations when tool schemas evolve.

title: GraphRAG: From Local to Global Query-Focused Summarization
abstract: GraphRAG constructs an entity knowledge graph from source documents and pre-generates community summaries to answer global sensemaking queries over large corpora.
main_finding: Hierarchical graph-based community summaries significantly outperform vector similarity search on corpus-wide analytical questions.

title: SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?
abstract: SWE-bench evaluates language models on 2,294 real software engineering tasks collected from popular Python repositories requiring multi-file editing and unit test validation.
main_finding: Real-world codebase navigation, long-context editing, and test-driven debugging expose major limitations in standalone LLMs.

title: Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback
abstract: Constitutional AI trains harmless AI assistants through self-critique and revision guided by an explicit list of normative principles rather than human red-teaming labels.
main_finding: AI-generated feedback guided by explicit principles achieves strong safety alignment while reducing evasive refusals.
